name: retailvest-smart-money
description: What hedge funds and famous investors own, buy and sell (SEC 13F, 13D/13G, Form 4), and how crowded futures markets are (CFTC), with sources.

interface.longDescription:
Explore public filings and futures positioning with RetailVest.

Ask which of about 250 tracked funds hold a stock and how much; what Berkshire Hathaway, Pershing Square, Appaloosa, or another tracked manager reported holding and changed last quarter; which stocks appear most often across fund portfolios; what funds bought or sold on balance; and about recent activist stakes (13D), passive 5%+ stakes (13G), and insider transactions (Form 4). You can also check how futures speculators are positioned in markets such as gold, oil, grains, and Treasuries.

Answers include reporting periods or filing dates and source links when available. 13F reports describe a manager's holdings at quarter end and may be filed up to 45 days later; they do not show current positions or necessarily represent an individual's personal account. CFTC reports show positions as of their stated report date; they are generally weekly and usually published Friday. Sign in with your RetailVest account to connect. The plugin is read-only and cannot place trades or change your account. RetailVest provides data and research, not investment advice.
defaultPrompt: What did Warren Buffett buy and sell last quarter?
Which well-known funds own NVDA, biggest holders first?
Is gold crowded among futures speculators right now?

positive.prompt: What did Warren Buffett buy and sell last quarter?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds Berkshire Hathaway's slug (warren-buffett), then lists the latest 13F holdings with weights and the quarter's new, added, trimmed and sold-out positions. Names both the reporting period and filing date, links the SEC filing when available, and clarifies that the filing is the manager's reported portfolio rather than Warren Buffett's personal account or current positions.

positive.prompt: Which well-known funds own NVDA? Show the biggest holders.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists tracked investors holding NVDA ranked by dollar value (e.g. Ken Fisher, MFS, Baillie Gifford, Loomis Sayles) with value, portfolio weight and reporting period. Makes clear these are reported quarter-end holdings, not live positions, and cites the relevant filing source when available.

positive.description: Consensus holdings and the quarter's clearest moves
positive.prompt: Which stocks do the most top investors own, and what did funds buy most this quarter?
positive.expected_behavior: Gives the most widely held stocks with fund counts and average weight, states whether the results use a common or mixed reporting period, then lists stocks bought on balance (more funds buying and net dollars in) with the funds behind them. Identifies the 13F reporting periods and explains these are SEC filing-based snapshots, not live activity.

positive.prompt: Any recent 5%+ stakes or insider trades by activist investors?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists recent 13D filings and Form 4 trades first (e.g. Carl Icahn, Barry Rosenstein), with stake percent or shares and price, filing date and lag from the event, and folds routine 13G batches into one line per filer. Links each SEC filing source when available and distinguishes filing date from event date.

positive.prompt: Is gold crowded among futures speculators right now? Which markets are most crowded?
positive.expected_behavior: Reports large speculators' net position in gold (net long or short and % of open interest), its rank against the last 26 weekly reports, this week's flow, and the CFTC report date. Identifies the CFTC Commitments of Traders as the source and makes clear this is weekly data, not live positioning.

negative.description: Personal investment advice is not provided
